answer: A prism-bound optical fingerprint stops one person holding many identities. At enrollment, a prism is scanned: laser light through its microscopic flaws makes a speckle pattern no factory can copy exactly, hashed to the identity. Each dawn, auditors wander through the registry, issue a random challenge angle, and require the speckle response within minutes. One fake needs a fabricated token, a reader, and an answer, so ten fakes cost ten of each, answered at once. Limits: readers exclude users and worn prisms drift, so re-enrollment audits and slashing for duplicated patterns are needed.
